wa_b_motherland.blurb: Motherland is a short wall of sport climbs in the Overhaul Area of the Far Side, in the Exit 38 climbing zone near North Bend. It lies between Relief Camp and the Slabbage Patch, a short stroll along the base from the first of those. All 14 routes are bolted, running from the 5.7 range up through the 5.10s and into several 5.12s, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. The lines are steep, overhanging and juggy, and the wall sits where the local rock changes character, giving a mix of textures. Expect a steep uphill walk on the final stretch of the approach.

wa_bird_watching_boulder_the.blurb: A tall freestanding boulder, around 80 feet high, in the Rocks of Sharon south of Spokane. Lines climb every side, so you can usually find either sun or shade. The 14 routes are mostly sport, with a few trad lines and one top rope, spanning roughly 5.6 to 5.12 with the bulk in the 5.10s and low 5.11s. The stone is described as very good, with plenty of pockets and knobs. It is a short walk from Big Rock: head east past the foot of the Rookie Wall and then the Gem Stone, and drop down a small trail for roughly three minutes.

wa_bookstore_main_area_the.blurb: The Main Area is the first section on the left at the top of the approach trail at the Bookstore, a cliff in the Kettle Valley near Curlew in Okanogan County. The face looks east from a long ridge and gets its name from a run of open-book corners. Routes here are chiefly trad, with a couple of sport lines, 14 in all, mostly between 5.7 and 5.11 with a good number of 5.8s and 5.10s. Pitches run from short to about 160 feet at the Bookstore as a whole. The hike up from the road takes around 10 minutes.

wa_pasture_the.blurb: A quiet bouldering zone on the Mountain Home Road hillside above Leavenworth, reached on foot a few minutes beyond the Star Wars boulders. It holds 14 problems that run from V0 up to the V11 and V12 range, with a fair spread in the middle, V1 through V5, and a few serious hard ones. The rock is sharp on the skin. There are few trees, so it sits in strong sun and feels hottest in the afternoon, and rarely gets crowded. Climbers get a view over Icicle Canyon and its creek. Cattleguard Arete and the other arete lines are the ones that draw people.

wa_b_snag_buttress.blurb: Snag Buttress is the prominent feature at the foot of the Main Wall on Mt Erie, near Anacortes. It is a compact stack of 14 routes, split between sport and trad, with one in the 5.7 range and the rest packed into the 5.10s and 5.11s, so it favours climbers comfortable with harder grades. The south-facing buttress takes sun from early morning into late afternoon. Many lines also lead up to Main Wall West above. Approach is about 10 minutes up the trail from the Main Wall lot to the ledge. Wear a helmet, as loose rock and ledges sit above.

wa_secret_dome.blurb: Secret Dome is a quiet slab crag in the Bebop-Dinky-Secret group along Icicle Creek, near Leavenworth. Its 14 routes lean to trad, with a few sport lines, and cover roughly 5.7 to 5.11, with plenty at 5.9 and 5.10. The climbing is slabby and technical, where footwork and balance count for more than strength, and it is a good place to sharpen slab skills. Walk in on the forested trail that starts across the road from 8 Mile Buttress; the base sits a few minutes beyond BeBop Rock. The trail can be overgrown.

wa_submarine_boulder.blurb: The biggest boulder in the Rattlesnake Lake area near North Bend, and the usual place to begin bouldering there. It has 14 problems on three of its four sides, from V1 through the low V2s and V3s up to a handful at V6 and V7 and one harder line. It is a flat walk of about five minutes from the car to the beach, where the boulder stands directly ahead. Its position on the lakeshore means the water level matters, so it is easiest to reach when the lake is low, and it draws plenty of onlookers.

wa_te_fiti.blurb: Te Fiti is a large sea stack standing amid the Cape Disappointment campground at the mouth of the Columbia River, with a smaller stack, South Te Fiti, just south. The 14 problems are all bouldering, from V1 to about V6, with a good number of V1s and V3s. The east sides have easy down-climbs, while the west side is steep, with vertical and overhung high balls. The basalt around the cape is often mossy, but some faces stay clean enough to climb.
